h.select_rule: Discard any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own current value, or whose condition merely disables or disconnects the edited component. From the rest, keep 10 with distinct mechanisms and field pairs, favouring those where an informed expert could plausibly bet on either direction.
h.strategy: Two patterns are banned because experts find them obvious: (1) conditioning on the current value of the same field being edited, which just restates that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one; (2) conditions that make the edited component unused, unreachable or inert. Instead, each hypothesis must link two DIFFERENT fields that interact through a non-trivial mechanism, such as substitution between parallel routes, a capacity already supplied elsewhere, one part acting as a bottleneck for another, or interference that turns a usually helpful edit harmful. No condition setting may appear in more than two hypotheses. Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the source of each idea. In each 'why', name the mechanism and explain why the opposite direction is also a priori plausible.

hyps.why: An identity shortcut on 0->3 makes the cell residual so the 2->3 branch only refines the signal, buffering the cost of shrinking it to 1x1.
When 2->3 is parameter-free, a 3x3 conv on the shortcut becomes a primary learned input to node 3 and adds more than when 2->3 is already a conv.
With a 3x3 conv already feeding node 3 from node 1, another 3x3 on 0->3 gives diminishing returns.
With 1->3 pruned, node 1 reaches the output only through 1->2->3, so a conv on edge 2 adds real depth instead of competing with a shallow bypass.
If 0->2 already applies a 3x3 conv, another 3x3 into node 2 duplicates capacity and yields a smaller gain.
A conv on 0->1 pays off only if node 1 is consumed downstream, and a conv on 1->2 both guarantees that and forms a deeper conv stack.
When node 1 is a conv output, a skip on 1->3 delivers a distinct processed feature to the output instead of a near-duplicate of the input.
With no direct 0->3 shortcut, a skip on 1->3 becomes the cell's nearest residual path and helps optimization substantially.
When 1->2 is pruned, node 2 holds only what edge 1 supplies, so pooling there turns the whole 2->3 branch into blurred raw input.
When 2->3 delivers only pooled features, a learned 3x3 on 1->3 becomes the main source of sharp discriminative features at node 3.
